body_es: AWS Direct Connect y AWS VPN son los dos mecanismos principales para conectar infraestructura on-premises con AWS. AWS Direct Connect establece una conexión de red dedicada y privada entre el datacenter del cliente y una instalación de AWS Direct Connect, ofreciendo ancho de banda consistente (1 Gbps a 100 Gbps), latencia reducida y predecible, y sin exposición a Internet pública. Es ideal para transferencias de grandes volúmenes de datos, aplicaciones sensibles a la latencia, y cumplimiento normativo que requiere conexiones privadas. Las conexiones Direct Connect pueden ser dedicadas (fibra física exclusiva) o alojadas (capacidad compartida a través de socios AWS). Una Virtual Interface (VIF) puede ser pública (acceso a servicios AWS públicos como S3), privada (acceso a VPCs), o de tránsito (con Transit Gateway). AWS Site-to-Site VPN crea túneles IPSec cifrados sobre Internet entre un Customer Gateway on-premises y un Virtual Private Gateway (VGW) o Transit Gateway en AWS. Es más rápido de implementar (minutos vs semanas) y económico que Direct Connect, pero sujeto a la variabilidad de Internet. Para el SAA-C03: Direct Connect para rendimiento y privacidad consistentes; VPN como solución de failover o para despliegues pequeños con presupuesto limitado; Direct Connect + VPN juntos para mayor disponibilidad y cifrado adicional.
body_en: AWS Direct Connect and AWS VPN are the two primary options for extending your on-premises network into AWS. AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated private network connection between your data center and an AWS Direct Connect location via a physical cross-connect. Connections range from 50 Mbps to 100 Gbps and provide consistent bandwidth, reduced and predictable latency, and traffic that never traverses the public Internet. Direct Connect connections can be dedicated (a single physical port leased by the customer) or hosted (shared capacity provided through AWS Direct Connect Partners). Virtual Interfaces (VIFs) define what the connection accesses: Private VIFs connect to VPCs, Public VIFs to AWS public services (S3, DynamoDB), and Transit VIFs attach to a Transit Gateway for multi-VPC connectivity. AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates IPSec encrypted tunnels over the public Internet between a Customer Gateway (your on-premises device) and a Virtual Private Gateway or Transit Gateway in AWS. VPN can be provisioned in minutes at low cost but performance depends on Internet conditions. For SAA-C03 exam scenarios: Direct Connect for compliance requirements, large data transfers, or latency-sensitive workloads; VPN for quick setup, small deployments, or as a Direct Connect failover path; combining both provides maximum availability with encrypted backup.
example_code:
# Create Virtual Private Gateway
aws ec2 create-vpn-gateway --type ipsec.1

# Attach to VPC
aws ec2 attach-vpn-gateway --vpn-gateway-id vgw-123 --vpc-id vpc-123

# Create Customer Gateway
aws ec2 create-customer-gateway \
  --type ipsec.1 \
  --public-ip 203.0.113.0 \
  --bgp-asn 65000
